images.title: File:Jackson Tower, Everett Avenue and 56th Street, Indian Village, Hyde Park, Chicago, IL (54826562398).jpg
images.author: Warren LeMay from Chicago, IL, United States
images.credit: Jackson Tower, Everett Avenue and 56th Street, Indian Village, Hyde Park, Chicago, IL
images.description: Built in 1925, this Renaissance Revival-style building was designed by Walter W. Ahlschlager to serve as a luxury apartment building. The building is clad in brown and red brick with terra cotta trim, large arched bays on the building’s east wing, which serve as windows into two-story window rooms inside large duplex apartments that overlook Jackson Park and the Museum of Science and Industry, a front corner courtyard with a gabled porte cochere at the main entrance with arched openings, corner quoins and trim, terra cotta-clad parapets, a four-story penthouse atop the central wing, double-hung windows, and large external fire escapes on the east and north facades. The building today serves as a residential condominium, and is among the many historic high-rise residential towers that can be found along Chicago’s lakefront.

images.title: File:Main Street, Bethlehem, PA (52421929075).jpg
images.author: Warren LeMay from Chicago, IL, United States
images.description: Built in the 19th Century, this Italianate-style building features a brick exterior, two-over-two and two-over-four double-hung windows, decorative stone lintels and stone sills, a bracketed cornice, and a first floor storefront with a metal awning with brackets. The building is a contributing structure in the Central Bethlehem Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1972, and expanded to include additional buildings in 1988.

images.title: File:North Clark Street and Waveland Avenue, Wrigleyville, Lakeview, Chicago, IL - Raising Canes, November 2021 - 2.jpg
images.author: Warren LeMay
images.description: Built in 1910, this Gothic Revival-style mixed-use building stands on an irregularly-shaped piece of land at the corner of North Clark Street and Waveland Avenue in Chicago’s Lakeview neighborhood. The building features a buff brick facade with triangular arches, a corner turret with decorative banded limestone trim, corbeling meant to resemble machicolations with long extruded brick pilasters, terminating at composite capitals, which extends along the facades facing Waveland Avenue and North Clark Street, limestone trim at the storefront, with fluted doric pilasters, decorative trim under the smaller windows of the North Clark Street facade, and decorative pressed metal window lintels over the larger windows. The building features a retail space on the first floor, formerly home to bars and currently home to a Raising Cane’s Chicken Fingers fast food restaurant, with an apartment unit on the second floor.

images.title: File:Wrigleyville, Chicago, Illinois (42488124325).jpg
images.author: Ken Lund from Reno, Nevada, USA
images.description: Formerly a working-class neighborhood, Wrigleyville is the nickname to the neighborhood directly surrounding Wrigley Field. The neighborhood is the namesake of Wrigley Field, home of the Chicago Cubs. Also known as Lakeview East, its borders run from north to south, Cornelia Avenue to Grace Street and from east to west, Wilton Avenue to Racine Avenue. Wrigleyville features low-rise brick buildings and houses, some with rooftop bleachers colloquially called Wrigley Rooftops where people can purchase seats to watch baseball games or concerts that, while generally more expensive than tickets for seats within the park itself, come with all you can eat and drink service. Proprietors are able to do so under special agreements with the Cubs organization. Many Wrigleyville bars and restaurants (particularly on North Clark Street) feature sports-oriented themes. Bars such as Sluggers, Murphy's Bleachers, Casey Moran's, Rockwood Place, Sports Corner and The Cubby Bear host the Cubs crowds near the Wrigley Field intersection of North Clark Street and West Addison Street. <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_View,_Chicago#Wrigleyville" rel="noreferrer nofollow">en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_View,_Chicago#Wrigleyville</a> <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Text_of_Creative_Commons_Attribution-ShareAlike_3.0_Unported_License" rel="noreferrer nofollow">en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Text_of_Creative_Commons_...</a>
